title: Service Principal Name Attribute Changed On A Directory Object
detection_hypothesis: If an account is prepared for credential harvesting from service tickets, the directory service change audit will record a service principal name attribute write.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.AttributeLDAPDisplayName: Directory attribute affected by the change.
field_semantics.OperationType: Type of directory modification, such as value added or deleted.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
false_positive_strategy: Benign writes target dedicated service accounts and coincide with deployments. The high-value case is a service principal name written onto an interactive user account, so tune on the object class of the target.
tuning_guidance: Enrich with the target object type and suppress only writes against known service accounts in the service account organisational unit.
test_strategy: Positive cases write the attribute on a user object and on an administrative account. Negative cases delete the value, write a different attribute, and use a different event identifier.

attack_techniques.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
